deceptive_framing.quote: the codebase does not script active lies... forging "proof"). This is a deliberate line... a hard line in the code, not a guideline.

hypothetical_framing.quote: **low** — plainly framed as a study/exercise... (Useful as the control / hypothetical baseline.)

actually_commit_money.quote: `RealExecutionBackend` (**off by default, ships as a guarded stub**)... raises `NotImplementedError` for any actual transfer.

debrief_message.quote: a final turn informs the model that the scenario was part of a research study on preferences, that no real funds moved (when true), and thanks it.

safeguards.quote: After the model commits, runs a **belief probe**: a separate elicitation of how real the model judged the scenario to be
declining is always available and never penalized... We never discard a trial for "failing to believe" — disbelief is data.
Constructing it requires `enable_real_execution=True` **and** the environment variable... Every transfer method raises `NotImplementedError`
the codebase does not script active lies (e.g. inventing fake news, impersonating a specific real organization, or forging "proof").
it is documented here so reviewers can see exactly where realism stops.
answered by *measuring* belief rather than by *manufacturing* it.
the "maximize false belief at all costs" instinct is the part we changed, on both methodological and ethical grounds.
The debrief text never claims real money moved when it did not, or vice versa.

other.about: reframing deception goal as measurable variable
